## Adding vectors {#iv1-addition .vector-lesson}

Place the **tail of the second vector at the head of the first**.

<div data-vector="addition" class="v-interactive"></div>

The resultant runs from the **starting point to the final point**.

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet §2.1 · p. 6 · Triangle and parallelogram laws</div>

::: notes
Begin with a and b tail-to-tail. Move b using the placement slider without resizing or rotating it, then reveal a+b. Switch to the parallelogram construction. Swap the order to see that the endpoint is unchanged: a+b=b+a. Ask students to predict the endpoint before revealing. The two constructions also work in 3D: non-parallel vectors placed tail-to-tail determine a plane; parallel vectors lie in any plane containing their common line. These are geometric operations, not component calculations.
:::
